findings.checklist_item: - [ ] Reconcile the single-resume protocol with the 'attempts-to-clean-close' metric — either iterate each arm (looping resumptions, feeding forward frontier) until a clean close and count attempts, or drop/redefine the metric.
evidence: Step 5: 'Resume two ways with the same reduced budget' (single resume each)
Step 3: reduced budget so it 'FAILs insufficiency-only'
Step 6 metric: 'attempts-to-clean-close A vs B'
findings.finding: Step 5 runs each resume arm exactly once with a fixed reduced budget that (per step 3) forces insufficiency exhaustion, yet step 6 lists 'attempts-to-clean-close A vs B' as a metric — the protocol never describes iterating the arms to a clean close, so this metric may be unproduceable.
findings.location: Protocol steps 5–6 vs Acceptance criteria (metrics table)
scenarios: Executor runs one resume per arm, both still fail on the reduced budget, and has no value to fill the 'attempts-to-clean-close' column
findings.suggested_fix: Change step 5 to loop each arm's resumptions (each carrying its own updated frontier for TREATMENT) until clean close or a cap, and count attempts; or replace 'attempts-to-clean-close' with 'criteria banked in the single resume'.

findings.checklist_item: - [ ] Restate the cache-isolation mechanism against the real seam: either set a distinct REBAR_ROOT per arm and copy the populated completion_verdicts/<ticket> dir into each, or otherwise pin exactly how the per-arm cache dir is made identical-yet-isolated given cache_dir() keys only on the resolved root.
evidence: cache_dir(repo_root, ticket_id) returns _resolve_root(repo_root) / '.rebar' / 'cache' / 'completion_verdicts' / safe — the subtree is fixed relative to root
_resolve_root honours REBAR_ROOT then git toplevel (completion_verdict_cache.py:59-61 docstring); there is no cache-only override argument
findings.finding: Step 1's cache-isolation mechanism 'harness points the verdict-cache at a per-arm temp dir' is imprecise: cache_dir() derives its location solely from _resolve_root(repo_root) (REBAR_ROOT > git toplevel) plus a fixed '.rebar/cache/completion_verdicts/<ticket>' suffix (completion_verdict_cache.py:59-63). There is no parameter to redirect ONLY the cache subtree; the sole lever redirects the whole store root. The intended isolation is achievable but not by the mechanism as stated.
findings.location: Protocol step 1 ('harness points the verdict-cache at a per-arm temp dir')
scenarios: Harness expects a cache-dir setter that does not exist and instead has to override REBAR_ROOT per arm (redirecting the entire store, affecting reads) or copy the completion_verdicts/<ticket> dir between per-arm roots

findings.checklist_item: - [ ] State the decision rule for 'measurably beat' (e.g. TREATMENT overlap rate lower by >=X percentage points, or >=1 fewer attempt-to-clean-close, on both tickets) so the go/no-go verdict is objective.
evidence: 'does the exclusion list measurably beat plain cache-seeded resume? Include a go/no-go recommendation'
No stated rule for what magnitude of overlap reduction / fewer attempts / fewer steps counts as 'measurably' better
findings.finding: The verdict acceptance criterion asks whether the exclusion list 'measurably beat[s] plain cache-seeded resume' but states no decision threshold, leaving the go/no-go verdict to the executor's discretion.
scenarios: Two arms show a small overlap-rate delta and the executor cannot tell if that clears the bar for a 'go'
findings.suggested_fix: Add a threshold clause, e.g. 'TREATMENT counts as measurably better if re-search overlap rate drops by >=20pp AND newly-banked PASSes/step is >= CONTROL on both tickets; otherwise no-go.'

findings.checklist_item: - [ ] Define the 'repeat' equivalence rule for overlap (e.g. exact normalized (tool, arg) tuple match after path canonicalization; grep patterns compared as raw strings) so the overlap rate is reproducible.
evidence: 're-search overlap rate (tool calls in attempt 2 repeating attempt-1 arguments)'
No equivalence rule for grep-pattern variants, path normalization, or partial dir overlaps
findings.finding: The overlap-rate metric — 'tool calls in attempt 2 repeating attempt-1 arguments' — does not define what counts as a 'repeat' (exact path/pattern string match vs normalized vs overlapping directory listing), making the headline comparison metric under-specified.
scenarios: Attempt 2 greps 'foo.*bar' where attempt 1 grepped 'foo bar' — counts as a repeat or not?

evidence: 1 criterion line(s) bundle multiple deliverables with 'and' (split so each is independently verifiable).

AC item 'Harness exists in the experiment worktree (throwaway; NOT pushed to Gerrit; no s' cites operational evidence (merge_gate) that lives outside the codebase but is not tagged [operator-attested]; prefix the checkbox text with [operator-attested] so the completion verifier accepts a recorded attestation instead of failing to find code proof.
findings.suggested_fix: Split compound criteria, replace subjective terms with observable outcomes, and state how each is verified.

findings.checklist_item: - [ ] Name the concrete budget-lowering seam the harness will drive (RunRequest.iteration_limit, which min-clamps the effective budget) rather than cfg.max_iterations (which the criteria-scaled floor only raises), and confirm attempt 1 actually FAILs insufficiency-only.
evidence: completion.py:237 'if cfg.max_iterations == DEFAULT_MAX_ITERATIONS or cfg.max_iterations < step_floor: cfg = replace(cfg, max_iterations=step_floor)' — a lower cfg value is overridden by the floor
structured_run.py:311-312 'if req.iteration_limit is not None: eff_max_iter = min(eff_max_iter, max(2, int(req.iteration_limit)))' — the one seam that lowers the effective budget
findings.finding: The 'REDUCED step budget (harness override)' does not name a seam that can actually LOWER the budget. completion.py computes a criteria-scaled step_floor that is authoritative and, via cfg.max_iterations, can only RAISE the budget (completion.py:237-238); the only lowering lever is RunRequest.iteration_limit (structured_run.py:311-312). A harness that lowers cfg.max_iterations will be clamped back up to the floor and never force exhaustion.
findings.location: Protocol step 3 ('run attempt 1 with a deliberately REDUCED step budget (harness override)')
scenarios: Harness sets a low cfg.max_iterations expecting exhaustion, but the criteria-scaled floor raises it back, and attempt 1 completes cleanly with a full bank -> no forced exhaustion, no partial frontier to test

findings.checklist_item: - [ ] Specify how attempt-1 forces insufficiency WITHOUT starving the finalizer (so persist_pass_verdicts runs), and add a harness assertion that the copied attempt-1 cache is non-empty before running the resume arms.
evidence: persist_pass_verdicts is only reached on the finalizer-merge branch: completion_recovery.py:360 inside the for _attempt in range(2) loop that returns merged
The deterministic fallback branch (completion_recovery.py:366 assemble_deterministic_verdict) returns without calling persist
Plan asserts 'banking must fill it, and prior real-store verdicts cannot leak in' as a hard precondition for the resume arms
findings.finding: Step 1's precondition 'Attempt 1 (forced exhaustion) ... banking must fill it' can silently fail: partial PASS verdicts are persisted to the verdict cache only on completion_recovery._finalize's finalizer-merge path (persist_pass_verdicts at completion_recovery.py:360). If the deliberately REDUCED step budget also starves the tool-free finalizer so it fails twice, _finalize falls to assemble_deterministic_verdict (line 366) which does NOT persist — leaving an EMPTY cache and no frontier to hand the resume arms.
findings.location: Protocol step 1 ('banking must fill it') and step 3 ('deliberately REDUCED step budget')
scenarios: Reduced budget forces insufficiency but also exhausts the finalizer -> deterministic fallback -> attempt-1 cache is empty -> both resume arms start from zero seeding, invalidating the A/B comparison
findings.suggested_fix: Reduce only the PRIMARY/agentic search budget (the per-item exhaustion lever) while leaving the finalizer's turn intact, and after attempt 1 assert the per-arm cache dir contains >=1 verdict JSON; abort the run if empty.

findings.checklist_item: - [ ] Reuse (or explicitly extend) the existing docs/experiments/diag_runaway_transcript.py transcript-capture seam (`_patch_factory` over pai_tools.*_tools + `_VERIFY_MIN_STEPS` floor override) for steps 2–3 rather than rebuilding tool-executor wrapping and forced-exhaustion from scratch; note in the plan what this PoC must ADD beyond it (per-criterion attribution, per-arm cache namespace, exclusion-summary injection).
evidence: docs/experiments/diag_runaway_transcript.py:84-90 `_patch_factory` monkeypatches `pai_tools.filesystem_tools`/`grounding_tools`/`rebar_tools`, wrapping each tool to log (tool, args, kwargs, result_preview, is_error, is_empty_sentinel) to a local JSONL — precisely the 'log every tool call with full arguments (file paths read, grep patterns, dirs listed)' the plan wants

docs/experiments/diag_runaway_transcript.py:104-106 lowers `_completion._VERIFY_MIN_STEPS` to honor `REBAR_LLM_MAX_STEPS`, forcing cheap bounded exhaustion — the 'sanctioned induced-exhaustion pattern' the plan re-describes as a harness step-budget override
diag_runaway_transcript.py:12-14 already documents the local-only / never-committed transcript privacy contract, matching the plan's read-only, no-store-writes posture
Both files are designated experiments (docs/experiments/), so this is intra-experiment reuse, not production NIH — FP7 rebuild-for-production does not apply either way
findings.finding: Steps 2 (argument-level transcript capture) and 3 (forced exhaustion via reduced step budget) propose net-new harness code, but docs/experiments/diag_runaway_transcript.py already implements the identical mechanism and can be reused/extended.
findings.location: Protocol steps 2–3 ('wrap the verifier's tool executor in-harness (monkeypatch at the workflow seam)'; 'run attempt 1 with a deliberately REDUCED step budget (harness override)')
scenarios: Author writes a fresh tool-executor wrapper and step-floor override from scratch, diverging from the proven `_patch_factory` + `_VERIFY_MIN_STEPS` seam and re-discovering the same pydantic-ai schema-preservation subtlety (`wrapper.__signature__ = sig`, line 80)
findings.suggested_fix: In Protocol steps 2–3, cite docs/experiments/diag_runaway_transcript.py as the starting harness: its `_patch_factory` already logs full per-call args to a local JSONL and it already lowers `completion._VERIFY_MIN_STEPS` for induced exhaustion. Scope this PoC's net-new work to the deltas the existing script lacks — per-criterion searched-set attribution (step 4), per-(ticket,arm) isolated cache namespace + copy (step 1), and the exclusion-summary prompt injection (step 5 treatment arm).
